name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
prevalence_note: RSCNPF White Collar Crime Unit, FSRC St. Kitts & ECCB (headquartered in Basseterre) 2025-2026: cloned WhatsApp 'stranded in the US' money-transfer & access-code scams, phony online escrow + remote-desktop scams, and ECCU bank/lottery frauds dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-869 within NANP and hosts ECCB headquarters; overseas scammers clone local WhatsApp accounts and spoof +1 numbers.

scams.name: RSCNPF-Warned Cloned WhatsApp 'Stranded Overseas' & Code Scam
scams.name_en: Cloned WhatsApp contact claiming to be stranded in the US and requesting money transfer or access codes
scams.signals_en: Overseas scammer hijacks or clones a local contact's WhatsApp account, claims to be stranded in the United States needing an urgent money transfer, or tricks contacts into approving unrequested access verification codes.
scams.legit_en: RSCNPF White Collar Crime Unit advises always calling the contact on a reliable voice line first and never approving unrequested verification codes.
bait_tactics: Insist on speaking by regular voice call or asking a personal Basseterre/Charlestown family question first.
Say the remittance counter is closed and ask which US airport terminal they are at.
Refuse to touch any verification code prompt on your screen.

scams.name: FSRC-Warned Phony Internet Escrow & Remote Desktop Scam
scams.name_en: Fake online escrow agent instructing buyer/seller to wire funds or install remote desktop software
scams.signals_en: Fraudster directs a high-value online buyer or seller to a fake escrow website or instructs them to install remote-desktop software to 'verify' the transaction while draining bank funds.
scams.legit_en: FSRC St. Kitts warns that legitimate escrow services never ask users to install remote-desktop tools or wire money to unverified accounts.
bait_tactics: Say your work laptop blocks all third-party downloads and ask for their FSRC licence details.
Tell them you will have your local solicitor in Basseterre verify the escrow company independently.
Pretend the escrow webpage fails to load and ask them to spell out the company registry name.

scams.name: ECCB-Warned Fake Lottery Prize & Bank Phishing Scam
scams.name_en: Fake sweepstakes advance-fee call or bank impersonator seeking card/OTP credentials
scams.signals_en: Caller claims the resident won a lottery requiring an upfront fee, pitches a zero-risk crypto pyramid, or poses as an ECCU bank requesting OTPs.
scams.legit_en: ECCB advises never paying advance fees for prizes, never sharing OTPs, and checking ECSRC licensing before investing.
bait_tactics: Ask why a genuine lottery cannot deduct its own fee before issuing the cheque.
Tell a supposed bank caller you will walk into the Basseterre branch directly.
Ask for the caller's ECSRC licence status and watch them stall.
